item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A correctional officer at Century Correctional Institution was assaulted by an inmate this week, according to the Florida Department of Corrections. Inmate Dwayne A. Collins grabbed the officer during the incident, but no staff members were injured in the altercation. Collins is serving a 30-year sentence for a 2013 homicide conviction out of…
item.content:encoded:
A correctional officer at Century Correctional Institution was assaulted by an inmate this week, according to the Florida Department of Corrections. Inmate Dwayne A. Collins grabbed the officer during the incident, but no staff members were injured in the altercation.

Collins is serving a 30-year sentence for a 2013 homicide conviction out of Highlands County. The circumstances surrounding the assault and any disciplinary action against the inmate have not been detailed by the FDC.

Century Correctional Institution, located in North Escambia County, houses adult male inmates and is part of Florida's state prison system.

item.content:encoded:
Atmore Police are investigating a shooting that occurred early Sunday morning at a large gathering on Carver Avenue, according to a Facebook post from the department. At least one man was shot during the incident at what police described as a party with approximately 500 people in attendance.

The shooting happened near the intersection of King Street and Sims Street in Atmore. Details about the victim's condition were not immediately available, nor did police provide information about potential suspects.

Atmore Police have not yet released additional details about the investigation. Anyone with information about the incident is encouraged to contact the Atmore Police Department.

item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida football team delivered another impressive statement in its Division I transition, dismantling No. 24 Central Arkansas 42-14 on the road Saturday night. The lopsided victory caps a dominant stretch for the Argos, who entered the contest ranked No. 25 in one major poll and are likely to climb both national rankings following the convincing performance.

According to reporting on the game, UWF's complete control on both sides of the ball against a ranked opponent suggests the young Division I program is moving faster up the competitive ladder than many expected. The road win—always tougher than home games—demonstrates the Argos can execute at a high level away from Pensacola.

The emphatic victory adds to the momentum surrounding UWF's historic jump to the FCS level. With several weeks of the season remaining, the Argos appear positioned to compete for bowl eligibility in their debut Division I campaign.

item.content:encoded:
A federal Homeland Security agent has turned himself in to Baldwin County authorities in Alabama, facing a slate of serious sexual assault charges. According to the Spanish Fort Police Department, Kent Blacklidge surrendered at the Baldwin County Jail on Saturday and is being held on charges including rape, sodomy, sexual abuse, and incest.

The charges mark a significant development in what appears to be an ongoing investigation by local law enforcement. Details surrounding the circumstances of the alleged offenses or their timeline have not been made public by authorities at this time.

Blacklidge's employment status with the Department of Homeland Security and any potential federal involvement in the case remain unclear. The Baldwin County case will likely draw scrutiny given the defendant's federal law enforcement background.

item.title: Wahoos Edge Clingstones 8-6 in 10 Innings, Magic Number Down to 3

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos stayed hot Friday night, grinding out an extra-inning victory over the Columbus Clingstones that keeps them firmly in control of their division race.

After a tight pitching contest through nine innings, the Wahoos broke through in the 10th to win 8-6. The victory extends Pensacola's lead over Columbus to 5.5 games with just eight regular-season games remaining.

With the win, the Wahoos' magic number—the number of wins they need combined with Columbus losses to clinch the division—dropped to 3. The team is positioned well heading into the final stretch of the season, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The Wahoos will look to keep the momentum rolling as they push toward the postseason.

item.title: Escambia Gators Hold Off Tate for First Win of Season
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Escambia had dropped its first two games without scoring before finding the end zone against Tate. The Gators' defensive effort kept the…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia High School Gators got off the shutout streak Friday night, edging the previously unbeaten Tate Aggies 6-3 in a defensive struggle that gave coach Mike Bennett his first victory of the season.

Escambia had dropped its first two games without scoring before finding the end zone against Tate. The Gators' defensive effort kept the Aggies' high-powered offense in check, limiting them to just a field goal in what turned into a low-scoring affair.

Tate, under coach Rhett Summerford, came in undefeated and looking to stay perfect through three weeks of play. The Aggies' offense, which had been prolific early in the season, couldn't find its rhythm against Escambia's defense on Friday.

The win marks a turning point for the Gators program as they look to build momentum heading into the rest of their schedule.

item.title: Hot, humid Labor Day weekend ahead with afternoon storm chance
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Plan for typical late-summer weather this Labor Day weekend across North Escambia, with highs climbing near 90 degrees and a solid chance of afternoon thunderstorms Saturday. According to the National Weather Service forecast, Saturday will bring a 50 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours, with mostly sunny skies…
item.content:encoded:
Plan for typical late-summer weather this Labor Day weekend across North Escambia, with highs climbing near 90 degrees and a solid chance of afternoon thunderstorms Saturday.

According to the National Weather Service forecast, Saturday will bring a 50 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours, with mostly sunny skies otherwise. Winds will remain calm throughout the day. If storms develop, rainfall could reach a quarter-inch or more in isolated areas, though most spots will see a tenth to quarter-inch of moisture.

Saturday night conditions improve slightly, with only a 20 percent chance of showers after 1 a.m. Those planning outdoor Labor Day activities should keep an eye on afternoon storm development but shouldn't expect significant weather disruptions overall.

Anyone with information about what happened is encouraged to contact the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

item.content:encoded:
Toby Moore, a worship leader and frontman for a Christian rock band based in Pensacola, is channeling his faith and passion for music as he navigates a diagnosis of terminal brain cancer. According to WKRG News 5, Moore has become an inspiration to those around him by maintaining his focus on serving others despite the serious health challenge he faces.

Moore's journey illustrates how some people in our community are finding meaning and purpose during life's most difficult moments. Rather than withdrawing from his calling, he continues his work leading worship and creating music—activities that have become central to how he processes his diagnosis and connects with his faith.

The Pensacola worship leader's story reflects the resilience of local faith communities and the role that music and spirituality play in helping individuals cope with profound adversity. WKRG's reporting highlights Moore's determination to maintain his ministry and relationships even as he manages the physical and emotional toll of terminal illness.

item.title: Diesel prices surge to record high, squeezing local farmers like Ryan Jenkins
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Diesel fuel has hit a record national high of $5.85 per gallon, breaking a record that had stood since 2022, according to AAA. The spike is hitting local farmers especially hard as they face mounting operational costs at a critical time. Jay farmer Ryan Jenkins says the jump is showing up directly in his bottom line. A single hauling trip to sell…
item.content:encoded:
Diesel fuel has hit a record national high of $5.85 per gallon, breaking a record that had stood since 2022, according to AAA. The spike is hitting local farmers especially hard as they face mounting operational costs at a critical time.

Jay farmer Ryan Jenkins says the jump is showing up directly in his bottom line. A single hauling trip to sell corn in Laurel, Mississippi, now costs him close to $900 in fuel alone—up from about $3.71 per gallon a year ago. The surge is largely driven by the ongoing conflict with Iran, which has disrupted global energy markets.

The timing couldn't be worse for Jenkins and other local agricultural producers. Farmers are still waiting on Congress to pass a new farm bill, something that hasn't happened since 2018. The current extension of that 2018 bill runs out September 30th, leaving producers in limbo.

The House passed its version of the farm bill in April on a narrow 224 to 200 vote, but the Senate Agriculture Committee hit a roadblock. The committee tried to advance its own version in August but couldn't get it out of committee, prompting the chairman to call an indefinite recess on the effort. Without further Congressional action, the current extension will expire at month's end, potentially leaving farmers without key support programs heading into 2025.

item.content:encoded:
WKRG News 5 is partnering with the Panini's Senior Bowl this season to showcase top high school football talent across the Gulf Coast region, according to reporting from the Mobile-based news station.

The collaborative coverage effort, called Senior Bowl Spotlight, will feature standout players like Velus Jones Jr. as part of a weekly series highlighting the area's best prep football prospects. Mobile and Baldwin County have long been breeding grounds for future NFL talent, making the partnership a natural fit for fans following the region's athletic development pipeline.

The Senior Bowl has a storied tradition of showcasing college players heading to the professional level, and this expanded high school coverage aims to give early recognition to the next generation of talent working their way through the system. For Northwest Florida sports fans, the series offers a way to track promising players who could eventually compete at the college or pro level.

item.title: Hall's Fine Meats Reopening in Chickasaw After Year-Long Fire Recovery
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Nearly a year after a devastating fire destroyed their original location, Hall's Fine Meats is preparing to reopen in Chickasaw with a fresh start at a new address. The family-owned butcher shop will operate from the corner of West Lee and Grand Streets, marking a significant rebuild for the longtime business. Co-owner Deborah Hodges told WKRG…
item.content:encoded:
Nearly a year after a devastating fire destroyed their original location, Hall's Fine Meats is preparing to reopen in Chickasaw with a fresh start at a new address. The family-owned butcher shop will operate from the corner of West Lee and Grand Streets, marking a significant rebuild for the longtime business.

Co-owner Deborah Hodges told WKRG News 5 that the new storefront represents more than just a relocation—it's a chance to revitalize that corner of town. "It's going to change the entrance to Chickasaw," Hodges said, expressing optimism about the relocated business and its impact on the community.

The fire that destroyed the original Hall's Fine Meats location left the family business without a home for months as they worked toward reopening. The move to the new location on West Lee and Grand Streets signals the completion of those recovery efforts and a return to serving customers in the area.

item.title: Fairhope Art Center Gets Vibrant New Wildlife Mural

item.content:encoded:
The Eastern Shore Art Center in Fairhope is adding another layer of creative expression to its campus with a freshly completed mural featuring local wildlife, according to WKRG News 5. The new artwork extends the gallery's mission beyond its interior walls, bringing color and visual interest to the center's exterior spaces.

The mural represents the art center's decades-long role as a community hub for creativity and artistic development. By featuring regional wildlife, the project connects local natural heritage with the visual arts—a fitting combination for a facility that's become a cornerstone of cultural activity on Alabama's Eastern Shore.

The addition is part of a broader trend of public art installations throughout the Gulf Coast region, where murals and outdoor artwork have become increasingly popular in downtown areas and institutional spaces. For Fairhope residents and visitors, the new mural offers another reason to stop by the art center and explore what's happening inside.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos are kicking off what they hope becomes an annual tradition by distributing books to every child in the pediatric unit at Studer Children's Hospital at Ascension Sacred Heart.

The gesture coincided with National Read a Book Day, with the team's mascot Kazoo visiting the hospital to hand out the books and interact with young patients. The initiative combines two community priorities: supporting children's health and encouraging literacy.

According to WKRG News 5, the Blue Wahoos are using their platform to make a direct impact on kids in the Pensacola area during their hospital stays. Hospital officials and the team haven't yet announced whether the book-giving will continue annually, but organizers framed it as the start of an ongoing commitment.

More details are expected as the situation develops.
